events.title: Country before the invented town
events.details: Indigenous peoples have lived on, cared for and travelled through the Macquarie–Wambuul basin for innumerable generations. The fictional town cannot be described as the first settlement or the land as previously empty of people.

events.title: Colonial expedition era
events.details: John Oxley travels the Macquarie region during the colonial period; this is not the discovery of Aboriginal land or the founding of Repository Town.

events.title: Railway reaches Dubbo
events.details: The Main Western railway reaches Dubbo in February 1881 and transforms freight and communications.

events.title: Rail extends west
events.details: The railway extension from Dubbo through Narromine towards Nevertire opens in October 1882. It supplies the realistic background for a fictional nearby goods village.

events.title: First permanent colonial-era building
events.details: Reginald Arthur Repo and Ellen Repo erect Repo's Stores, a timber slab general store, cart shelter and dwelling at what the game later calls G8-N. This is the first **fictional colonial-era permanent building**, not the first structure on Country.

events.title: Carted water and an unreliable well
events.details: Water is carried by horse cart and stored in barrels and tanks; an attempted shallow well has variable yield. Exact bore and water rights are not invented.

events.title: Road and stockyards
events.details: A rough wool-and-grain track connects the store, railway corridor and pastoral farms; fenced stockyards and a farrier appear.

events.title: Repo's Halt nickname
events.details: Farmers petition for a railway loading point dubbed Repo's Halt; an actual historic railway siding at these coordinates is **not** asserted.

events.title: Local trading settlement
events.details: Bakery, smithy and cart repair shed appear; drought, dust and impassable muddy approaches shape building forms.

events.title: Dry years and water rationing
events.details: A dry spell prompts additional corrugated-iron tanks, hand carts and careful storage. This specific 1892 town event is fictional.

events.title: Repository becomes the place-name
events.details: Repo's Cross Roads gradually becomes Repository on traders' notices, named for its early stores and the Repo family.

events.title: First classroom
events.details: Ellen Repo helps arrange a part-time schoolroom used between shearing and harvest seasons; no real NSW school registration is implied.

events.title: Local fire volunteers
events.details: Residents stock leather buckets, water drums and horse-drawn pumping gear at the store; modern emergency agencies arrive much later.

events.title: Federation celebrated
events.details: Local residents gather to mark the real Federation of Australia in a fictional community meeting.

events.title: High Street surveyed in town lore
events.details: The fictional grid is laid out with a high street, wider crossing avenues, drainage reservations, civic plot and farm roads. No actual NSW deposited plan is claimed.

events.title: Progress committee
events.details: Repo's committee finances basic roads, dust control and shared drinking-water storage. Real government in the region is separate.

events.title: First mayor Reginald Repo
events.details: Reginald Arthur Repo becomes **Repository Town's first in-universe mayor** of its fictional council. This does not create an actual separate NSW local government area at the real anchor.

events.title: First building replaced by public hall
events.details: The 1883 Stores are carefully dismantled and timber reused in a larger hall on the G8-N plot, explaining the current Town Hall heritage plaque.

events.title: NSW country hotel architectural comparison
events.details: An independently documented NSW country hotel dates to 1911; this is comparative architectural context only. The Merged Branch at N8-S has an UNKNOWN original construction date.

events.title: Regional hotel trade context
events.details: Regional Australian hotels served travellers in this era. This 1912 context does NOT date Repository Town's pub, whose first trading year remains UNKNOWN.

events.title: War and absence
events.details: The First World War affects local labour, farming and community life; do not invent named historical casualties.

events.title: Community memorial fund
events.details: Families hold a fictional memorial fundraiser and maintain a register of returned residents, without impersonating real records.

events.title: Small generator and street lamps
events.details: A local fuel-fired engine supplies limited evening electricity to the hall, pub and a few shops; household use remains sparse.

events.title: Sir Reginald title
events.details: An entirely fictional knighthood recognises Reginald's community philanthropy. In 1909 he was **not yet Sir**; later chroniclers use the title retrospectively.

events.title: Depression public works
events.details: Unemployed tradespeople repair culverts and unsealed lanes. Council cuts night lighting and postpones buildings.

events.title: First sealed high street
events.details: Bitumen reaches the shop frontage, while rural access roads remain mostly unsealed.

events.title: Founder's death
events.details: Sir Reginald Repo dies in the fictional story; his name survives on the hall's honour board and road signs.

events.title: Wartime freight and supplies
events.details: Wartime rationing, supply convoys and farm production affect the community; no real military installation is attributed to the parcel.

events.title: Flood preparedness
events.details: A documented regional history of floods prompts the fictional town to plan evacuation and protect low-lying approaches.

events.title: Macquarie basin flood
events.details: The historic major flood at Narromine becomes the regional design lesson; there is no measured water depth at the selected coordinate.

events.title: Mid-century hospitality fit-out comparison
events.details: A mid-century hotel bar refit is a plausible design reference, NOT evidence that The Merged Branch was refurbished in 1958.

events.title: Water and sewers upgraded
events.details: A fictional treated water network and gravity sewer are introduced in stages. Real intake, wastewater outfall, licences and pipe locations are unresolved.

events.title: Burrendong Dam completed
events.details: Regional Macquarie flows are influenced by the real upstream dam; it does not eliminate flood, supply or drought risk.

events.title: Modern electricity begins
events.details: The township transitions from independent generation to regional distribution; no actual year of connection or named feeder at the parcel is claimed.

events.title: Freight outlives passenger service
events.details: Local station activity becomes mostly goods-oriented. The game's rail platform and timetable are fictional even though the regional railway is real.

events.title: Older brick shopfronts retained
events.details: Residents preserve timber awnings and brickwork amid new materials, without a claimed legal heritage listing.

events.title: Hospitality refrigeration comparison
events.details: Late-twentieth-century refrigeration improvements inform the fictional pub kitchen; NO 1988 renovation is established for this building.

events.title: Flood and drought resilience
events.details: Sheds, tanks and raised equipment racks feature in local disaster planning, but parcel flood elevations remain unknown.

events.title: Telephone and early internet
events.details: Businesses adopt computers and dial-up, using fictional customer accounts rather than invented historic telephone exchange maps.

events.title: Council works yard modernised
events.details: The rural depot gains fleet storage, salvage stock and maintenance facilities.

events.title: Energy and street-lighting renewal
events.details: Old luminaires are progressively replaced, with inconsistent coverage retained in older streets.

events.title: Repair and recycling sector
events.details: The town develops reuse, recycling and skills activities that later become its 2026 circular economy.

events.title: Present-day pub naming reference
events.details: The Merged Branch is the current fictional venue name. The naming or renaming year and its original trading name are UNKNOWN; 2019 is contextual only.

events.title: Pandemic disruption
events.details: Shops revise service, health communications and supply chains in response to the global event; no fictional exact case numbers are assigned.

events.title: Macquarie catchment flooding
events.details: Regional severe wet-weather risk leads to renewed drainage and warning planning; the selected parcel's actual flood condition is unverified.

events.title: Digital work orders
events.details: Town Hall starts electronic service requests and infrastructure maintenance records.

events.title: Trades, digital and civic growth
events.details: Education, computing and repair/reuse facilities expand within the game's 234-site plan.

events.title: Mayor Vern and democratic life
events.details: Vern is the current playable mayor, challenged by Arlo and Sadie. Seven-game-day elections are gameplay compression, not actual NSW election cycles.

events.title: Pub utility and sanitary gameplay pilot
events.details: The Merged Branch has modelled WC, kitchen, electricity, refrigeration and water systems; its construction date is UNKNOWN and compliance is not certified.

events.title: Town mapped to Central West NSW
events.details: The game gains a deliberate anchor at -32.273600,148.408400 on a candidate rural footprint west of Minore. Real ownership, cadastral and network access clearance remain unverified.
